name: APR FC

coach.name: Vincent Mashami
coach.bio: A former Amavubi assistant, Mashami built his reputation on compact, high-tempo football. He has turned APR into the league's most relentless pressing side.

description: Rwanda's most decorated club and the reigning Rwanda Premier League champions, based at Amahoro Stadium in Kigali.

name: Rayon Sports FC

coach.name: Adil Mohammed Erradi
coach.bio: Erradi favours possession with vertical intent. The Moroccan coach is known for developing young attackers and for his detailed set-piece work.

description: Kigali's biggest community club, with a fierce rivalry against APR and one of the largest supporter bases in East Africa.

name: Kiyovu Sports

coach.name: Jimmy Mulisa
coach.bio: A former Amavubi striker, Mulisa has made Kiyovu one of the league's most organised defensive units while giving academy graduates regular minutes.

description: One of Rwanda's oldest clubs, founded in 1958, and a fixture of Kigali football for more than six decades.

name: AS Kigali

coach.name: Eric Nshimiyimana
coach.bio: Nshimiyimana's teams are compact in midfield and dangerous from wide areas. He led AS Kigali to the 2023 Peace Cup final.

description: The city council-backed club from Kigali, known for a strong youth pipeline and a passionate following at Kigali Pelé Stadium.

name: Police FC

coach.name: Christian Ndayishimiye
coach.bio: Ndayishimiye preaches discipline and quick transitions. Police are among the fittest sides in the league and rarely beaten late in games.

description: The Rwanda National Police club, a top-flight regular with a gritty, organised identity.

name: Mukura Victory Sports

coach.name: Etienne Ndayiragije
coach.bio: Ndayiragije has brought a direct, aggressive style to Huye. Mukura are especially strong at home and dangerous on the counter.

description: Based in Huye, southern Rwanda, Mukura are perennial cup contenders and have one of the country's most loyal travelling supports.

name: Musanze FC

coach.name: Sosthène Habimana
coach.bio: Habimana's side play with the energy of the northern hills: hard running, aerial power and a fearless approach to away games.

description: The pride of northern Rwanda, playing their home games near the foothills of the Virunga volcanoes.

name: Gasogi United

coach.name: Olivier Mucyo
coach.bio: Mucyo is one of Rwanda's most promising young coaches, building a brave, front-foot team around homegrown talent.

description: A fast-rising Kigali club founded in 2012, promoted to the top flight and now establishing itself as a serious cup side.

name: Bugesera FC

coach.name: François Hitimana
coach.bio: Hitimana has built Bugesera around a stubborn back line and rapid wing play, making Nyamata a difficult away trip.

description: Eastern Province's leading club, representing Nyamata and the wider Bugesera district.

name: Gorilla FC

coach.name: Thierry Hitimana
coach.bio: A young coach with a modern data-led approach, Hitimana wants Gorilla to press high and play through midfield.

description: A youthful Kigali side with a bold brand and a growing following among the city's next generation of fans.

name: Amagaju FC

coach.name: Pascal Nduwimana
coach.bio: A veteran of Rwandan football, Nduwimana leans on experience and set-piece organisation to keep Amagaju competitive.

description: A Huye-based club with a strong community identity and a reputation for producing combative midfielders.

name: Etincelles FC

coach.name: Aimé Nshimiyimana
coach.bio: Nshimiyimana has kept Etincelles in the top flight with a resilient away-game plan and smart use of loan players.

description: Western Province's historic club, founded in 1954 and based in the lakeside town of Rubavu.

name: Marines FC

coach.name: Jean-Bosco Nduwimana
coach.bio: The former defender demands aggression in duels and has made Marines one of the league's toughest teams to break down at home.

description: The Rwanda Defence Force-affiliated club from Rubavu, sharing Umuganda Stadium with Etincelles.

name: Rutsiro FC

coach.name: Emmanuel Nshimiyimana
coach.bio: Nshimiyimana's young squad plays without fear, though inconsistency has been their biggest obstacle this season.

description: One of Rwanda's newest top-flight clubs, carrying the hopes of Rutsiro district in Western Province.

name: Vision FC

coach.name: Jean de Dieu Mukunzi
coach.bio: Mukunzi is a development specialist, giving teenagers meaningful minutes in a league that rarely trusts youth.

description: A Kigali club built around youth development, with an emphasis on players from the city's academies.

name: Kirehe FC

coach.name: François Ndayisaba
coach.bio: Ndayisaba has built a direct team that uses the size of Kirehe Stadium well, though travel form remains a concern.

description: Eastern Province's second representative in the top flight, based in Kirehe near the Tanzanian border.

name: Amavubi

coach.name: Torsten Spittler
coach.bio: The German coach took charge of Amavubi in 2024 after years of development work in Rwanda. Spittler has prioritised a compact block, quick wingers and giving the country's best young players a platform.

description: The Rwanda national football team. Known as Amavubi — 'the wasps' — Rwanda play their home games at Amahoro Stadium.

name: Benin

coach.name: Gernot Rohr
coach.bio: The Cheetahs are coached by the vastly experienced Gernot Rohr.

description: Benin national football team, the Cheetahs.

name: Lesotho

coach.name: Leslie Notsi
coach.bio: Lesotho's Likuena are a compact, hard-working side.

description: Lesotho national football team, Likuena.

name: South Africa

coach.name: Hugo Broos
coach.bio: Bafana Bafana are coached by Hugo Broos.

description: South Africa national football team, Bafana Bafana.

name: Tanzania

coach.name: Hemed Morocco
coach.bio: Taifa Stars are coached by Hemed Morocco.

description: Tanzania national football team, Taifa Stars.
